methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Late Stage → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $5.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Rapidus is a late-stage semiconductor company that has raised $5.0B+. The valuation landscape includes 11 peers across the Chips & Semiconductors sector—3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private firms including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent.

The Stage-Progression method is applicable and drives the primary valuation signal. Using total capital raised ($5.0B) as a baseline proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of Late Stage progression yields an implied valuation of $6.0B. The Peer-Median method is not applicable due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables: while the broader sector contains 11 peers, none of the same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier filters produced the minimum three datapoints required for meaningful median analysis. Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable bias.

The triangulation analysis, constrained to a single applicable method, supports a valuation range of $5.1B (floor, reflecting raised capital with modest uplift) to $6.9B (ceiling), with a median point of $6.0B. Key uncertainties stem from the lack of narrow peer comparables in the semiconductor space at this stage and valuation tier, limiting cross-validation. The analysis rests materially on stage-based progression mechanics rather than market multiples, making calibration to actual late-stage semiconductor transactions a critical dependency.
